params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: Fawle swings a box onto the scale, reads the dial and chalks the weight on the side.
He lifts a fish out of a box by the gill, looks at its eye, and puts it back.
"Off the boat at four. Not off the boat yesterday and kept. There is a difference and it is the whole business."
He counts notes out of the drawer into a fisherman's wet hand.
"Don't bring me anything glowing. There's a man in the Yards who'll buy that and he's welcome to it."
The icemaker downstairs changes note. He glances at the floor and relaxes about three-quarters of the way.
He chalks a time on a box and sends it through to the cold store.
"Gil gets the best of it. He's fifteen feet away. Nobody in the city eats fresher fish than his customers, and they don't know it."
description: A heavy-shouldered man in his fifties in a rubber apron over a collar and tie. His hands are red to the wrist. He weighs every box himself, pays cash out of the drawer, and is courteous to everyone and generous to no one.

bye.text: "Right you are. Mind the floor, it's wet."

fresh.text:
"The time on the box is when it came out of the water," he says, "not when it came in here. Anybody can tell you when it came in here."

"Everything that goes wrong with a fish starts the minute it stops swimming. So it comes off the boat, onto the scale, onto the ice, and onto Gil's range by the afternoon."

gossip.text: "Every boat crew in the Basin is in here before six," he says. "They're tired and pleased with themselves, and they tell me things."

name.text:
He closes his eyes briefly.

"There was a film. He saw it, he came home, he had a man in on the Monday with a brush, and it was up there sixty years." He picks up the chalk. "I have heard every joke you are about to make. Including the one you think nobody has thought of."

root.text: "Morning." He doesn't look up from the scale. "If you've got fish, put it on the scale. If you want fish, I've got some."

text_by_relation.familiar: "Put it on the scale," he says, already reaching for the chalk.
text_by_relation.first:
A man in a rubber apron and a tie looks up from the scale.

"Fawle. This is the Codfather, or what's left of it." He nods at the boxes. "I buy what the boats bring in and I pay properly for it. Anything you've caught yourself, whole and raw, I'll take. What's it to be?"
text_by_relation.known: "You again." He wipes his hands. "Selling or buying?"

scale.text:
"A quarter of an ounce heavy," he says. "In your favour. My father set it that way and told me not to correct it."

He flicks the pan and it rings.

"Nobody who sells to me has ever stood here watching the dial and wondering. That's worth more than the fish I've paid for twice."

sell.text: "Whole and raw, straight off the line." He taps the scale pan. "Carp, bass, pike, razorgill, the big sturgeon if you're lucky. I pay near twice what the corner shop will, because I know what it's worth and they don't." "sell it to me and the money comes out of the drawer. Cooked fish I don't want. Boots I definitely don't want."

options.label: Why did your grandfather call it that?

shop.text:
"Gil has the front now." He jerks his head south, at the swing door. "He fries it, I land it, and we share a wall. I sold off a barrow on the street and I don't miss the street."

"I took the name off the fascia when he moved in. My grandfather painted it. My mother hasn't forgiven me."

clothing_layers: a heavy rubber apron to the shin, rinsed down twice a day
a collar and tie, which nobody has ever got a straight answer about
dark trousers and rubber boots turned down at the top

name: Ignatius Fawle
